keyVerseText: And there stood up one of them named Agabus, and signified by the spirit that there should be great dearth throughout all the world: which came to pass in the days of Claudius Caesar.
rootMeaning: The name Ἄγαβος (Ágabos) is of Hebrew origin, linked to the root חָגָב (Châgâb), which means 'locust.' This root word also identifies a family leader among the returned exiles with Zerubbabel, suggesting a heritage marked by restoration and God's providence. The literal sense of 'locust' evokes imagery of both destruction and divine judgment, adding depth to the personal name beyond a mere identifier.
usageInScripture: The term Ἄγαβος appears only twice in Scripture, both times as a proper noun translated consistently as 'Agabus.' This consistency indicates that the word functions solely as a personal name rather than a common noun or metaphorical term. The two occurrences highlight Agabus as a notable Israelite figure within the early Christian narrative, emphasizing his role rather than any lexical variation.
theologicalSignificance: Understanding Ἄγαβος as rooted in a Hebrew term meaning 'locust' enriches our appreciation of the biblical character Agabus, who serves as a prophetic voice in the early Church. His name, connected to an image of judgment and divine intervention, aligns with his role in foretelling a coming famine, demonstrating God's sovereign control over history. This reminds believers that God often uses individuals with distinct callings to communicate His purposes, underscoring the continuity between Old Testament imagery and New Testament fulfillment. Recognizing the Hebrew origin of his name also affirms the unity of Scripture and God's unfolding redemptive plan through Israel and the Church.
keyVerseReflection: Acts 11:28 records that 'one of them named Agabus' stood up and, through the Spirit, predicted a severe famine affecting the whole world. The use of the name Agabus here grounds the prophecy in a real, historical person, emphasizing the authenticity and divine inspiration of the message. Knowing the meaning behind his name adds a layer of solemnity to the warning, as it echoes the biblical motif of locusts and judgment, reminding believers that God's warnings through His servants are both serious and trustworthy.
